ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, and through point $A$, $DA\perp AC$ intersects $BC$ at point $D$. If $\angle B=2\angle BAD$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BAD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since AB = AC, \\
it follows that $\angle B = \angle C = 2\angle BAD$, \\
hence $\angle ADC = \angle BAD + \angle B$, \\
since $\angle B = 2\angle BAD$, \\
it implies $\angle ADC = 3\angle BAD$, \\
given DA $\perp$ AC, \\
thus $\angle DAC = 90^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle ADC + \angle C = 90^\circ$, \\
it follows that $3\angle BAD + 2\angle BAD = 90^\circ$, \\
hence $\angle BAD = \boxed{18^\circ}$.
